practice_span: I have been in the workshop since I was thirteen. It has been forty years.
craft_description: I say it is a panchaloha idol made by lost-wax casting. To children I say, each idol is born only once.
craft_distinct: Each mould is broken, so no two identical idols exist in the world.
motif_meaning: Nataraja's ring of fire. It is the cycle of the universe. The golden glow of panchaloha is the true colour.
motif_story: I made a Nataraja for a temple. In the procession people pointed at the flames of the ring and prayed.
colour_change: Earlier only the natural gold. Now some ask for an antique finish. The alloy has not changed.
specialisation: Expression in the wax. I taught wax work to women in my workshop.
known_for: People come to me for the faces and eyes of temple idols.
craft_keep_change: I would keep lost-wax casting. I would change the middleman's price.
local_belonging_phrase: “Without Kaveri soil there is no idol of ours. Our ancestors came here for that soil.”
place_belonging_feeling: Kaveri soil gives our idols life. That is the pride.
ecological_input: The alluvial silt of the Kaveri bank is very fine for the mould. We make the wax with beeswax and resin.
place_use_moment: I brought silt from the Kaveri bank and coated the Nataraja mould with it.
place_missing: Without good silt the mould cracks and the fine lines do not come.
place_change: Water in the Kaveri has reduced and sand has been taken away. Now we must go far to get good alluvial soil.
place_before_after: Earlier silt was on the riverbank itself; now we must go far for it.
emotion_about_place_change: “If the river dries, the temple idol dries too. Nobody believes me when I say this.”
teacher_name_relation: My father, Ramalinga Sthapathi. I learned wax work from my uncle.
teaching_memory: For a whole year my father let me only roll wax. One day he melted a hand I had made and said, “Your fingers are not speaking yet.”
remembered_phrase_gesture: “Measure in the hand, devotion in the heart.” He would measure with a coconut palm leaf and fold it to show me.
family_generations: My grandfather, my father, me. My son Karthik studied engineering and came back. I can name seven generations.
family_line: Grandfather → father Ramalingam → me → son Karthik.
transmission_strength:
The wax method and the proportions are learned by eye in the workshop every day.

The meaning of the Shilpa Shastra verses. The habit of learning them by heart has declined.
teaching_practice: First I teach only rolling wax, then the proportions.
teaching_scene: We sat by the furnace. I folded the palm-leaf measure in Karthik's hand to show him.
teaching_difficulty: One idol takes months. Few young people come forward to learn patiently for years, and pay comes slowly.
primary_material:
Panchaloha (copper, brass, lead, silver, a little gold), beeswax, resin, alluvial soil.

Soil from the Kaveri bank. Copper and brass from the Kumbakonam market. Beeswax from the hill areas.
first_contact: As a boy I sat by the furnace rolling wax. I remember its smell and its warmth in my palm.
material_special: The alluvial soil mould holds even the wax's thinnest lines. So even the idol's fingernail comes out clearly.
material_in_hands: The right wax softens in the warmth of the palm, but doesn't melt. A line drawn on it stays as it is.
material_spoke: If wax sticks to the finger or cracks, the mix is wrong. A change in the metal's colour and sound also tells me.
correction_action: I add a little resin or oil to the wax and heat it again. If I doubt the mould, I stop the pour.
piece_time: A month and a half for a one-foot idol. Never rush the mould drying.
material_change: Pure beeswax and good silt have become scarce.
material_change_reason: Sand mining and less water in the Kaveri are the reasons.
material_change_gain:
Electric tools made the final finishing easier. Lifting heavy idols has become safer too.

Fine chisel work is declining. Pure beeswax and good soil are hard to get.
occasion_of_use:
Temple processional deities and home worship idols. Now we also make them for art galleries.

In a festival procession, the nadaswaram, incense smoke, and amid the garlands the Nataraja we cast seems to dance in the lamplight.
use_importance: “Only when it leaves the hand does an idol become a god.” The elders of our town say this.
use_feelings: Making a temple idol there is devotion and responsibility.
special_vs_everyday: A temple idol must follow Agama rules and proportions. A decorative idol may take some freedoms.
special_object_rule: Eye-opening of a temple idol is done last, at an auspicious time, only by the sthapathi. Until then it isn't a god.
special_missing: Without the processional deity, the festival procession cannot happen.
not_for_sale_example: The proportion notes for moulds made for temples, and our family's palm-leaf manuscript.
why_protected: They carry a faith handed down for generations. If those proportions reach the wrong hands, the idol's sanctity itself comes into question.
safer_alternative: The wax method, the soil coating, videos of casting. These can be shown to workshop visitors.
pride_source: Seeing people pray to an idol I made is my pride.
pride_moment: I first saw the Nataraja I cast in a temple procession. Nobody knew my name. People were praying to it. That is enough.
recognition_by_others: The temple priest, and then my father. He touched the idol's finger and said, “Fine.”
loss_if_stopped: A thousand-year-old Chola method would be gone in one generation. It would not come back.
loss_picture: Factory idols in temples, and the furnace cold in the workshop.
key_stakeholder_of_loss: Temples and devotees, and the families in town who depend on this work.
craft_hours: Eight hours a day, from wax to polish. Before a festival we work at night too.
change_in_lifetime: Before, temple work was the most. Now overseas and home-decor orders are more, and demand for small idols has grown.
artisan_initiated_change: For the first time, I am teaching wax work to women in my workshop. I also started direct selling with my son.
desired_keep:
Lost-wax casting, Kaveri soil, and the Shastra proportions.

Middlemen deciding the price, and the idea that this work isn't for women.
strength_anchor: The palm-leaf proportions are in my hands. Bringing expression into wax and casting without flaws are my strengths.
concern_anchor: Machine-made, sand-cast idols are being sold under the Swamimalai name. Good alluvial soil is also running out.
shareable_content:
The wax method, casting video, my name, workshop visits.

The palm-leaf manuscript, secret alloy proportions, and agreements with temples.
desired_change:
Proper permission to take alluvial soil, and a clear mark that sets fake idols apart.

A temple idol will be made only by lost-wax and by Shastra proportions.
learning_story: Once I poured metal into a mould that had not dried fully. The mould burst, three months of work were lost, and my hand was burned. Now I don't pour without tapping the mould and listening.
emotional_story: When we broke the mould, my father was sitting beside me, at an age when his hands shook. The face inside had come out clear. He said nothing, and wiped his eyes.
clarification_story:
A customer asked for two idols, exactly alike. I explained that each mould is broken, so no two identical idols exist in the world.

Many think this is a factory casting from a mould. Each idol is born only once.
